clue.text: Occupation or job curtailed by court hearing?

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the word for job loses its final letter

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a session is a sitting of a court, the period when it hears cases

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up their line of work, or a job cut short by a legal hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Possession and occupation both mean holding and living in a property, as in taking possession of a house.

clue.text: Extra support gaining cheers

indicators.note: gaining says the first piece picks up the next one tacked on after it

parts.note: a leg is a support, as on a table or chair
cheers is an informal goodbye, and bye is a short form of goodbye

explanation.surface: An additional backer arrives and wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leg bye is a run scored when the ball hits the batsman's body rather than the bat; it counts as an extra, not to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bye is one of the cricket extras, runs added to the total but not credited to any batsman.

clue.text: Crazy snooker shot expert gets on top of

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on top of means coming first, above the other piece

parts.note: crack as an adjective or noun means first-rate, an expert, as in a crack shot
a pot is a shot that sinks a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A wild shot on the snooker table, and an expert getting the better of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective describes wildly eccentric or foolish ideas, so it is a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Local language I used in sadness, husband having departed

indicators.note: used in means the single letter is put to work inside the other word
the husband having departed means his letter leaves the word for sadness

parts.note: pathos is a quality that evokes sadness or pity

explanation.surface: A widow speaks of grief in her regional dialect after her husband has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having departed' takes H from PATHOS to leave PATOS, and 'used in' puts I inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional dialect, the local speech of a particular area as opposed to the standard tongue.

clue.text: Rouse start of play and a TV broadcast with energy

parts.note: Act I is the opening act, the start of a play

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Stirring viewers with the first act of a drama shown energetically on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate something is to set it going, which matches rouse in the sense of stirring into action.

clue.text: Get away to hunt, missing end of shift

indicators.note: missing says a letter is lacking from the word for hunt

parts.note: to shoot is to hunt game with a gun

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone escaping a hunt while skipping the end of their work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of shift' gives T, which goes 'missing' from SHOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an exclamation telling a person or animal to go away, so it stands for get away!

clue.text: Begin support to take care of individual

indicators.note: taking care of something suggests holding it safely within, so the word for individual sits inside

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar, as of a bridge
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Starting to support a carer who looks after one person.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to be first to develop or launch it, so it is a verb close to begin or initiate.

clue.text: Scaremonger arranged photo op for me, suppressing Democrat

indicators.note: suppressing suggests holding something down inside, so the letter is enclosed
arranged means set out in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A politician's handler sets up a photo opportunity while silencing a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns PHOTO OP FOR ME into PROPHETOFOOM, and 'suppressing' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet of doom predicts disaster at every turn, so the phrase describes a scaremonger who spreads alarm.

clue.text: Almost everyone unenthusiastic about hot drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around the letter

parts.note: cool means unenthusiastic, as in a cool reception
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody is lukewarm about a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' and 'about' are the two indicators; 'hot drink' looks like the definition, but 'hot' is only the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is used loosely for any intoxicating drink, as in banning alcohol from a venue.

clue.text: Be very definite; store wealth for redistribution

parts.note: to lay down wine is to store it for the future

indicators.note: redistribution means sharing out again in a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to bank one's riches so they can later be shared out more fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down the law is an idiom for stating rules dogmatically, being emphatic and insistent.

clue.text: Old company chief recalled origins of unusual cookery company: a meat dish

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for chief is read backwards

parts.note: a boss is a chief or head

indicators.note: origins of picks out the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A former company head looks back on how an odd catering firm began, and its meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns BOSS into SSOB; 'origins of' gives U and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Osso bucco is an Italian dish of veal shanks braised in wine and stock, a classic meat dish.

clue.text: Climbing plant concealing golden key

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so the plant's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: ivy is a climbing evergreen plant
or is the heraldic term for gold, so it means golden

explanation.surface: A creeper hiding a gold key among its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with ivory, so an ivory is informally a key on a piano.

clue.text: Expedition experiences odd bits of trek

parts.note: to have something is to experience it, as in have fun

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and so on letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A party on an expedition goes through scattered stretches of a long trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of TREK, T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean speed or promptness in doing something, an older sense matching haste.

clue.text: It is a chop going off, becoming light green

indicators.note: a chop going off has gone bad and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spoiled pork chop turning a pale greenish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistachio names a pale yellowish-green shade, after the colour of the nut's kernel.

clue.text: Norwegian city's celebration of tools?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a hammer is a tool; the plural is the setter's whimsy on a festival of tools
a fest is a festival or celebration

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Norwegian town's name means a festival for tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of the clue order: 'celebration of tools' is a tool fest, read as HAMMER then FEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammerfest is a town in the far north of Norway, one of the world's northernmost towns.

clue.text: Journey aboard explosive naval weapon?

indicators.note: aboard means inside a vessel, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A trip on a ship carrying explosives and a naval weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of the British submarine-launched nuclear missile, and Neptune's three-pronged spear, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Shocking vote — not all plutocrats represented

parts.note: to elect is to choose by voting

indicators.note: not all means the last letter is left off the word

parts.note: plutocrats are the rich, people who rule by wealth

explanation.surface: A scandalous election in which only some of the wealthy elite are represented.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric can describe something that gives an electric shock, so shocking in the literal sense.

clue.text: Sailor boasted beside ship

indicators.note: beside means next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, meaning boasted
man means a ship, as in man-of-war or merchantman

explanation.surface: A sailor bragging while standing by his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN for ship comes from names like man-of-war and merchantman.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewman is a member of a ship's crew, so an ordinary sailor.

clue.text: Wary socialists accepting quiet development in publishing

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the soft letter sits inside

parts.note: coy can mean reluctant or wary of committing oneself
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
the left are socialists, the political left wing

explanation.surface: Cautious left-wingers grudgingly accept a quiet change in how books are published.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyleft is a licensing practice letting others freely copy and adapt a work, a modern twist on copyright in publishing.

clue.text: Good to slot in better suggestion about delicate control

indicators.note: to slot in means to fit a piece into a gap, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: finer means better
a tip is a suggestion or hint

explanation.surface: A good idea for slotting in a better suggestion on fine handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingertip is used for precise, sensitive handling, as in fingertip control of a car.

clue.text: Pedant uncovered source of amusement

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a stickler is a pedant, someone who insists on exact rules

explanation.surface: A fussy pedant exposed, to everyone's amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' takes off the outer S and R of STICKLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickle is a light touch that makes someone laugh, and figuratively anything amusing.

clue.text: Some lowlife recalled throttling constant hanger-on

indicators.note: throttling means grasping round the neck, so the letters close round the constant
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible, dishonest person, a piece of lowlife
c is the constant for the speed of light in physics

explanation.surface: A low criminal, called back, strangles a persistent sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns HEEL into LEEH, and 'throttling' wraps it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite, so figuratively a person who clings to others for profit.

clue.text: Poet maybe not worried over line one associated with Hardy

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the next
not here means without, so the word for worried is taken away

parts.note: laureate as in Poet Laureate; a poet is one kind of laureate
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A calm poet ranks above a writer linked with Thomas Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not worried' strips ATE from LAUREATE; 'over' puts LAURE above L. Hardy misleads toward the novelist; it is Oliver Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was the comedy partner of Oliver Hardy in the double act Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: Regular soldiers had an effect in sphere of action

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers rather than officers
bit, as when brakes bit, means took hold or had an effect

explanation.surface: Ordinary troops making an impact in their field of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbit can mean the range of someone's influence or activity, as in within his orbit.

clue.text: Poor pub that's some way down one's list?

parts.note: a bar is a pub

parts.words: that's some way down one's list?
parts.note: E is the fifth letter, so a pub labelled E is fifth on a list

explanation.surface: A shabby pub that sits low on someone's list of places to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BAR E, the pub ranked E, fifth on a list ordered A, B, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means scanty or meagre, as in a bare living, so it matches poor.

clue.text: Vibrant military chief mostly calm about our following

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, a military chief

indicators.note: about means around, so the trimmed word wraps around the other letters
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lull is a calm period
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A flamboyant commander, mostly calm about our following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' and 'about' both work on the word for calm; 'our' is taken as written, and 'following' supplies its abbreviation alongside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourful describes something lively and full of interest, as vibrant does.

clue.text: Like fighting in a marriage, taking sexual attraction the wrong way

indicators.note: taking here means having one part replaced, the attraction going in reversed

parts.note: marital means relating to marriage

indicators.note: the wrong way means read backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Married life turns combative when sexual attraction goes awry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word for married with two letters swapped: 'taking' and 'the wrong way' mark that the attraction inside it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means relating to war or combat, as in martial arts.

clue.text: Regular occupants of farm refuse to return tool

indicators.note: regular occupants are alternate letters, here the first and third
to return means to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: waste is refuse, rubbish

explanation.surface: The usual residents of a farm decline to give back a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular occupants of' gives F and R from FARM; 'to return' turns WASTE into ETSAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine saw with a narrow blade for cutting curves in wood.
